taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Odufor, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model from the published survey:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The paper labels this station's curve as AK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Odufor, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the paper's curve-type label does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note — Station Odufor, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation resolves a four-layer earth model. Layer 1 is a thin (0.14 m), low-resistivity topsoil at 20.32 ohm-m, likely moist clayey/organic cover. Layer 2 (851.16 ohm-m, 1.10 m thick) is a resistive sandy horizon, underlain by Layer 3, a thick (15.80 m) and highly resistive unit at 2511.9 ohm-m, interpreted as dry to coarse sand/gravel. Layer 4, from 17.04 m downward, drops to 1345 ohm-m and is the most promising water-bearing horizon; its base was not resolved by the sounding.

Curve type: resistivities increase 20.32 < 851.16 < 2511.9 (A), then peak and fall 851.16 < 2511.9 > 1345 (K), giving **AK**. This agrees with the published AK-type label.
